title: Assessing citation integrity in biomedical publications: corpus annotation and NLP models

extracted.subtask_description: Builds a labeled corpus and models for automatically detecting whether a citing sentence's claim is accurately supported by its cited reference article, via an eight-category annotation scheme collapsible to a 3-way SUPPORT/REFUTE/NEI scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACCURATE - citation context consistent with evidence segment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The citation context is consistent with an evidence segment in the reference article.' There exists a sentence/segment in the cited paper that entails the citing sentence's claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONTRADICT - citation context contradicts reference
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The citation context contradicts a statement made in the reference article.' The cited source actively says the opposite of what's claimed. A major error, taking precedence over any minor-error label.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOT_SUBSTANTIATE - relevant reference fails to back the specific claim
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The citation is relevant to the content of the reference article but the cited reference fails to substantiate all statements made in the citing paper.' Topically on-target, but the specific claim isn't actually backed by anything in the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common real-world failure mode: right paper, wrong/absent evidence. Distinct from IRRELEVANT - 'the right paper but no actual evidence for this specific claim' is a materially different and probably more common failure mode than 'wrong paper entirely.'

rubrics_metrics.name: IRRELEVANT - no information in reference bears on claim
rubrics_metrics.description: 'There is no information in the reference article relevant to the citation.' Wrong source entirely; nothing in the cited work bears on the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: OVERSIMPLIFY - findings oversimplified or overgeneralized
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The findings of the reference article are oversimplified or overgeneralized.' The cited evidence is real but the citing sentence stretches it beyond its actual scope/conditions - e.g., turning a conditional/qualified finding into an unconditional one.

rubrics_metrics.name: MISQUOTE - numbers or percentages misquoted
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The numbers or percentages are misquoted.' A specific quantitative distortion category, kept separate from qualitative oversimplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: INDIRECT - reference is not the original source
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The evidence segment includes a citation to other articles, indicating that the reference article is not the original source.' The cited paper is itself just citing someone else for the evidence (secondary/chained sourcing), mirroring the 'indirect reference' category found in the medical quotation-accuracy literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: ETIQUETTE - ambiguous citation style
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The citation style is ambiguous and it is unclear what is being cited from the reference article.' A citation-practice/clarity problem (e.g., citing an entire paper for a specific number) rather than a truth-value problem per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collapsed 3-way mapping for claim-verification modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Support = ACCURATE + INDIRECT (indirect/secondary sourcing is still counted as 'supported,' just flagged for provenance, not truth). Refute = CONTRADICT + NOT_SUBSTANTIATE + OVERSIMPLIFY + MISQUOTE + ETIQUETTE. Not Enough Information = IRRELEVANT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Refute bucket lumps genuine contradiction together with overgeneralization, quantitative misquotation, and mere citation-style ambiguity into one bucket - a modeling simplification worth flagging if reusing this mapping, since these are substantively different failure types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major-error precedence over minor-error labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme is organized hierarchically: one 'accurate' label, three major-error labels, and four minor-error labels; if a citation instance qualifies for a major-error label, that takes precedence over any minor-error label in annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-sentence retrieval as the labeling bottleneck
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence-sentence retrieval (finding which sentence(s) in the cited paper are the relevant evidence) achieved only κ = 0.20 (phase 1) → 0.37 (phase 2) agreement, and accuracy-label assignment (choosing among the 8 categories) κ = 0.18-0.31, both far below the κ = 0.96 for citation-context identification (finding the sentence(s) that constitute the citing claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even trained domain-expert annotators achieve only fair agreement on fine-grained accuracy labeling and on locating supporting evidence within a long source. Oracle condition (given gold evidence sentences) reaches Macro-F1 0.78 vs. realistic-retrieval Macro-F1 0.52, showing most of the current performance ceiling is bottlenecked by evidence retrieval, not the final support/no-support judgment itself.
